b: p

They’d been fishing most of that rainy cool November 3 day without much luck. Brandyn Steeger and his buddy John Ortiz were targeting salmon migrating out of Lake Michigan and into the Milwaukee River to spawn.
p
Mixed with the salmon were autumn-run brown trout that also were pushing out of the big lake and into the river.
p
It was getting near dusk that afternoon, and still the anglers had not hooked a fish.
p

Brandyn Steeger had been tossing a spoon most of the day but had just changed to a one-ounce minnow-imitating chrome lipless crankbait. He used bait-casting tackle, 20-pound test braided line with a 15-pound test fluorocarbon leader.
p

“I’d just cast my lure out when I saw a buck deer across the river, so I stopped my retrieve to make a video of it and that’s when a fish hit my plug as it was sinking,” 26-year-old Steeger tells Wired2fish. “I got a strike as the lure was falling in a slow-moving 15-foot-deep pocket of the river.”
p
Steeger says his adrenalin was flowing so much that the fish fight didn’t seem long. He also was yelling to his pal John to bring the landing net.
p

“John was a long way downriver, and I had to yell my loudest to get his attention,” said Steeger from West Bend, Wis. “He finally saw me playing a fish and came running back with the net – slipping and falling because of the rain and mud alongside the river bank.”
p

Ortiz got to Steeger as he worked the trout near the Milwaukee River shore, and scooped the fish into their net. The two men struggled to land the fish that was so heavy it bent their landing net handle.
p
The fish measured 32 inches in length, but they didn’t measure its girth or get a weight of the trout.
p
“It was heavy, and we figured it at least 15 pounds, maybe more,” Steeger said.
p
They quit fishing and took the trout home where it was filleted and eaten.
p

“I fried some fillet portions of my trout in butter and served it over rice,” said the angler. “It was fantastic, one of the best fish I ever ate, and I still have some in my freezer, and so does John.”
p

Steeger has thought about getting a replica mount made of his huge brown trout. But he says there are other, even bigger brown trout being caught now in the rivers along Wisconsin’s Lake Michigan shoreline.
p

“This has been a really good year for huge brown trout in and around Milwaukee,” he explained. “I was lucky enough to catch a nice one, but there are some bigger fish that I’ve seen other anglers catch.
p
“I think luck was with me because the day before I caught my trout, it was my birthday.”
